articles.title: Kawasaki Z650 S Launched in India at Rs 7.59 Lakh
articles.excerpt: Kawasaki India has launched the Z650 S at Rs 7.59 lakh ex-showroom, with new styling and a TFT display on the same 649cc twin. Here is what changed and what did not.
blocks: Kawasaki India launched the Z650 S on 3 November 2026 at **Rs 7.59 lakh ex-showroom**, with deliveries starting the same day, according to Autocar India and Auto India Daily. It is a restyled version of the Z650 naked motorcycle with a colour TFT screen, and it keeps the same 649cc parallel-twin engine. Kawasaki lists the model as the Z650 S (2027) on its India website. This article is current as of 3 November 2026.

The Z650 S costs Rs 33,000 more than the standard Z650, which the reports price at Rs 7.26 lakh ex-showroom. Ex-showroom means the price before registration, insurance and other charges, so the on-road price will be higher and will differ by city.

For buyers comparing the two versions on paper, the trade-off in the published figures is simple. The Z650 S adds a larger set of styling and display changes for Rs 33,000, while the standard Z650 keeps larger brake discs and is 5kg lighter. Whether those differences matter in daily riding is not something these reports can say, because they are launch summaries and not road tests.

The sources also agree that the engine, gearbox and torque figure are carried over. In plain terms, a 649cc parallel-twin has two cylinders side by side, and the six-speed gearbox is the same one used on the standard model, so the performance numbers on paper are essentially the same.

Z650 S: Rs 7.59 lakh ex-showroom
Standard Z650: Rs 7.26 lakh ex-showroom (as reported)
Difference: Rs 33,000
Colour: one option, White/Green

The engine is unchanged from the Z650: a 649cc parallel-twin with a six-speed gearbox. Autocar India and Auto India Daily both give 68.25hp and 64Nm of torque. Another outlet, AutoX, lists 67bhp at 8,000rpm, so the power figure differs slightly between reports; the torque figure is the same. Kawasaki's own India page did not show full specifications for the model when checked.
Because the engine is the same, the reports describe the Z650 S as a styling and technology update, not a mechanical one.

Styling: Kawasaki's Sugomi design language, with a new headlight and tail-light that the reports say resemble those of the Z900, plus updated bodywork
Display: a 4.3-inch TFT instrument screen with smartphone connectivity and turn-by-turn navigation
Accessory: a quickshifter is available as an optional extra
First reports also mention traction control
Not every change is an addition. According to Autocar India, the Z650 S has smaller brake discs than the standard Z650:

Front discs: dual 272mm, against 300mm on the Z650
Rear disc: 186mm, against 220mm on the Z650
Kerb weight: 193kg, against 188kg on the Z650, which is 5kg more
The suspension is largely unchanged: an RSU (right-side-up) fork at the front and a back-link monoshock at the rear.

Autocar India earlier reported the global unveil of the Z650 S, with repositioned foot pegs, a taller handlebar and almost entirely revised styling, and a UK price of GBP 7,199. Those international details have not been confirmed for the Indian model by Kawasaki India, so treat them as background.

The reports do not give tyre details or the warranty terms, and they do not name direct rivals. Readers who want the full specification and the on-road price in their city should check Kawasaki India's website or a dealer.
How to read the launch figures

Launch articles quote the manufacturer's numbers, and small differences between outlets usually come from rounding or from different units. Horsepower (hp), brake horsepower (bhp) and PS are close but not identical units, which is one reason 67bhp and 68.25hp appear in different reports. When figures matter for a purchase, the manufacturer's brochure and the dealer's quotation are the documents to rely on.
This is a news summary from published reports and the manufacturer's website, not a road test. Prices and figures are as of 3 November 2026 and may change.

articles.title: Honda Names Its India Electric SUV ALPHA: Debut 2 Dec
articles.excerpt: Honda Cars India has named its first electric SUV for India the ALPHA and said it will debut on 2 December 2026. What is confirmed, and what is not yet announced.
blocks: Honda Cars India has announced that its upcoming electric SUV will be called the **Honda ALPHA**, with its global debut in India on **2 December 2026**. The announcement came on 3 November 2026, according to Rushlane and Autocar India. Honda has not announced a price, range or battery size. This article is current as of 3 November 2026.

Name: Honda ALPHA, for the company's first electric SUV for India
Debut: 2 December 2026, in India
Production: Honda's Tapukara plant in Rajasthan
Background: the SUV is the production version of the 0 Alpha concept shown at the Japan Mobility Show in 2025

Toshiyuki Yanagisawa, President and CEO of Honda Cars India, said the name reflects the company's push to bring advanced electric mobility to Indian buyers while keeping its focus on quality, reliability and driving enjoyment, as quoted by Rushlane. Reports say the name draws on the first letter of the Greek alphabet and signals a new beginning.

Honda used its redesigned H mark in Honda Cars India's official communication for the first time with this announcement. According to the reports, the ALPHA will be the first Honda model in India to carry it. Honda's website shows a teaser page for the ALPHA under its future-mobility section.

Rushlane reports that India will serve as Honda's global production base for this model and that the SUV will reach India before other markets. Testing across India began in March 2026 and covered highways, city traffic, rough surfaces, varied weather and charging infrastructure checks.
Honda has not published the following, so any number seen elsewhere is a report or an estimate:

Price and launch (on-sale) date
Battery capacity and driving range
Motor power and drive layout
Full feature list

Autocar India says two battery options are expected, roughly 65 to 75 kWh, and a single front motor. It labels these as expectations, not confirmed figures. It also notes that spy pictures of test vehicles show a large central touchscreen and a separate digital driver display, while the final cabin has not been shown.
Debut is not the same as launch

A debut is the first public showing. A launch with prices and deliveries usually comes later. Honda has said a 2 December debut; reports describe a sales start in 2027, but Honda has not confirmed that date in the sources checked for this article.

Rushlane notes Honda's 2026 launches so far include the City facelift in May, the ZR-V hybrid in July and the Elevate facelift in October, and that Honda plans 10 new models in India by 2030, including seven SUVs. It also reports Honda Cars India's October 2026 domestic sales at 7,609 units.

Manufacturers often reveal a model's name weeks before its debut. The name tells readers little about the vehicle itself; the useful facts come on debut day, when a company normally shows the final design, battery and feature list. Until then, anything beyond the name, the date and the plant is a report about test vehicles or an estimate by a journalist.

Readers comparing electric SUVs should therefore wait for Honda's own specification sheet. Autocar India lists the Mahindra BE 6, Hyundai Creta Electric, Tata Sierra EV, Maruti e Vitara and Toyota Ebella as electric SUVs already on sale or expected in the same space, but a fair comparison needs Honda's official range and price, which do not exist yet.

For ordinary readers the practical points are short. The ALPHA is an electric SUV, so it will be charged from a plug or charger instead of filled with fuel. Honda has said it is built in India, and Rushlane notes that the testing included charging infrastructure checks, which is the part of an electric car's use that depends most on where a person lives.
Everything beyond the name, the debut date and the plant is unconfirmed until Honda's 2 December event. This page will not be updated.

articles.title: Royal Enfield Himalayan 750 Unveiled: Specs and Colours
articles.excerpt: Royal Enfield unveiled the Himalayan 750 at EICMA 2026 with a new 743cc twin. Official specifications, colours and UK prices, plus what is not yet known for India.
blocks: Royal Enfield unveiled the **Himalayan 750** at EICMA 2026 in Milan on 3 November 2026. It is powered by a new 743cc air-oil-cooled parallel-twin engine. UK and European prices have been announced with bookings open; an Indian price has not. This article is current as of 3 November 2026.

Royal Enfield's India product page for the Himalayan 750 lists the engine as a 743cc air-oil-cooled twin with a six-speed gearbox and electric start. The page gives 55 PS at 7,000rpm and 63Nm at 5,000rpm. BikeWale's report of the unveil gives 54.25bhp at the same engine speed; the two figures are the same power expressed in different units and rounding (PS and bhp are slightly different units), so a small gap is expected. Royal Enfield also says 90 per cent of peak torque is available from 3,500rpm, according to BikeWale, and the bike has an assist and slipper clutch.

Frame: box-section spine frame with the engine as a stressed member (BikeWale)
Suspension: Showa 43mm upside-down fork with 190mm travel; Showa rear monoshock with 175mm travel
Wheels: 19-inch front and 17-inch rear, tubeless, with 110/80 R19 and 150/70 R17 tyres
Brakes: twin 280mm front discs and a 255mm rear disc, with dual-channel ABS
Dimensions: 205mm ground clearance, 815mm seat height, 1,522mm wheelbase
Fuel tank: 17.8 litres
Kerb weight: 224kg, with 90 per cent fuel and oil

On electronics, the official page lists five riding modes, traction control, cruise control, tyre pressure monitoring and a 4-inch round TFT display. BikeWale adds that the bike has a six-axis IMU for cornering ABS and lean-sensitive traction control, Bluetooth with navigation, a new LED headlamp and two USB Type-C ports.

Five colours are listed: Antarctic Silver, Siberia White, Aztec Green, Viking Bronze and Tectonic Black. BikeWale reports that Antarctic Silver is shown with a touring package of top box, hard panniers, heated grips, hand guards and a skid plate.
BikeWale reports these UK prices, with bookings open in Europe, and gives rupee equivalents that are only conversions:

Alloy-wheel variants: GBP 6,999
Spoked-wheel variant: GBP 7,299
Antarctic Silver with luggage package: GBP 8,699

Royal Enfield's India page states no ex-showroom price. BikeWale says it expects an Indian launch at the Royal Enfield Motoverse, held 26 to 28 November 2026, but that is the outlet's expectation, not a company announcement.

Royal Enfield also showed the Continental GT 750 at EICMA 2026. BikeWale reports that it uses an uprated version of the same 743cc twin and comes in faired and unfaired versions, with a twin-pod TFT cluster and the colours Red Line, TT Blue and Master Clean. Power, torque, weight and price for that model had not been published in the sources checked, so none are given here.

The Royal Enfield page gives power in PS, a metric horsepower unit, while many news reports use bhp. One metric horsepower is about 0.986 of a brake horsepower, so 55 PS and 54.25 bhp are close to the same quantity but are not identical numbers. The torque figure of 63Nm is the same in both sources, and so are the capacity and the engine speeds.

The kerb weight of 224kg is measured with 90 per cent fuel and oil, according to the company's page, which is a common way of stating a ready-to-ride weight. It is a published figure for comparison, not something tested here.

A spine frame uses a strong central beam, here a box section, to join the steering head to the rear of the bike, and using the engine as a stressed member means the engine itself carries part of the frame's load. Royal Enfield's description, as relayed by BikeWale's report, is the reason the Himalayan 750's weight is said to be close to that of the company's 650cc engine. The torque spread claim, 90 per cent of peak from 3,500rpm, refers to how early in the rev range the engine produces most of its pulling force.
Figures here come from Royal Enfield's own page and a news report on the day of the unveil. Check Royal Enfield for any later changes.
